interpretation: Two necessary scope controls for the proposed hybrid-block co-design, not new architectures. Same augmented data, ordered identities, optimizer, seed, steps and two already-observed development orders as the four-arm reference. Parameter counts are near-matched; ranks and feature allocations differ. Changing only one parameter pathway can still affect downstream hidden states and other memory layers. Any success weakens a claim that both selected component types must be adapted; failure alone does not establish unique memory storage or semantic write damage. No fresh-confirmation or universal-superiority claim. Six models share the same 12 underlying validation event streams. Paired counts are descriptive, not six independent datasets. Good component-only answers weaken a joint-adaptation necessity claim only for the tested group, training budget and tasks; poor answers can reflect fit or capacity.
